title: Getting to Know You Conversation Cards
teachingNote: Pairs ask three questions, then introduce each other. Use “She works…” and ask one follow-up question.

title: Daily Life Conversation Cards
teachingNote: Use go, turn, cross, and transfer. Have the listener repeat the directions to check understanding.

title: Daily Life Conversation Cards
teachingNote: Practice confirming the day and time. Add “Can you repeat that?” and repeat the details back.

title: Community Conversation Cards
teachingNote: Recommend a place, then adapt the follow-up: “What are you interested in doing there?”

title: Consumer Smarts Superlative Game
teachingNote: Choose just one category. Compare two options, then explain which is best and why.

title: Housing Ranking Game
select: Apartment features: most to least important
teachingNote: Rank the apartment features. Add “We have to…” or “We don’t have to…” where it fits. Accept different priorities with reasons.

title: Housing Conversation Cards
teachingNote: Role-play a repair call. Add the week’s pattern: “I need to report a problem. I want to know when someone can come.”

title: Workforce Conversation Cards
teachingNote: Turn experience into job-application sentences. Teacher adaptation: add one “Before I…, I had…” sentence after the basic task.

title: Workforce Conversation Cards
teachingNote: Practice a short follow-up call. Teacher adaptation: “I have already interviewed. I haven’t heard back yet.”

title: Career Awareness Conversation Cards
teachingNote: Revisit gross pay, deductions, and benefits from W25. Use “Tax is taken out” and explain one line in plain English.

title: Health Conversation Cards
teachingNote: Use fictional names and details. Practice “I have a sore throat” and “I’d like to make an appointment.” This is speaking practice, not a medical-advice activity.

title: Health Conversation Cards
teachingNote: Ask when a prescription will be ready and repeat the answer. Optional teacher follow-up: “If I had called earlier, I would have known.”

title: Wellness Conversation Cards
teachingNote: Discuss a realistic short break. Teacher adaptation: add a small milestone with “By Friday, I will have…”; the original game does not teach this tense.

title: Future Goals Conversation Cards
teachingNote: Choose three helpful tips. Add one example of progress from this year; students can use familiar language before trying a new tense.
